//: The ApexX-only half of the grammar. `scripts/build-grammar.mjs` merges these rules into the vendored Apex grammar and splices the includes below into the Apex rules named by `inject`, so everything Apex already colours keeps its own scopes.

repository.//0: A lambda, signature and body together. The body has to be inside the rule rather than left to the surrounding expression: a `{` reached from an expression is an array initialiser in Apex, so a block body's `return` would not be a keyword. Ending on `(?<=\})` closes a block body and `(?=[;,)])` an expression body, and because the block is consumed whole by `#block`, punctuation inside it never ends the lambda early.
repository.//1: `(account, other) =>`. The lookahead keeps this off an ordinary parenthesised expression, which is the rule that would otherwise claim the same open paren.
repository.//2: `account => account.Name`, the form the collection helpers take.
repository.//3: `Func<Account, Boolean>`. Func is an ApexX built-in, so it is scoped like one; its arguments are ordinary types.
repository.//4: A tuple type, `(String, Decimal)`, wherever a type is expected -- including nested in `Map<Id, (String, Decimal)>`.
repository.//5: The ApexX List methods. Apex would colour these as any other call; scoping them as built-ins is what marks them as part of the language rather than the class.

//6: Where the rules above are spliced into the Apex grammar. `before` names the first existing include to sit in front of; the ApexX rule has to win the race for a token that both grammars could claim.
